text: Boccaccio's Decameron was among the works burned in Florence in 1497, in a bonfire incited by Girolamo Savonarola. It was placed on the Index of 1559 under the instructions of Paul IV, and its prohibition was confirmed in the Index of 1564. In 1573 Pope Gregory XIII commissioned a revised edition in which the clergymen were replaced with secular people.
meta_description: Boccaccio's Decameron was burned in Florence in 1497, placed on the Index in 1559 and revised in 1573 at the order of Pope Gregory XIII.
